data.name: Help_Settings_GameSafeMode_Risk
data.value: LLT can't promise that a game won't flag it: only the anti-cheat makers decide that. This mode avoids what anti-cheats are known to look at. While it's on, the OSD shows fewer readings (no power, voltage, VRAM or disk temperatures), and macros and the Caps Lock / Num Lock pop-ups don't work. The PawnIO driver stays loaded; LLT just stops using it. Vanguard decides by itself at boot whether that driver may load.

data.name: Help_Settings_GameSafeMode_What
data.value: LLT checks every few seconds whether the service of Riot Vanguard (vgc), Easy Anti-Cheat or BattlEye is running; these normally run only while a protected game or its launcher is open. LLT only asks Windows for the service status and never looks at the game itself. While one runs, LLT pauses detailed sensors (no readings go through the PawnIO driver), pauses macros (they send simulated key presses) and removes its keyboard hook for Caps Lock and Num Lock pop-ups. The OSD keeps running on readings that need no driver: CPU and GPU temperature, usage, clock and fans from Lenovo's own sensors, memory from Windows, and FPS from Windows' frame-timing events. Everything comes back when the game closes.

data.value: Keeps the LLT window above other windows, including while you work in another app.

data.name: Help_Settings_Animations_What
data.value: Full adds movement and live effects, Reduced keeps only fades, Off turns animations off. Windows' "Animation effects" setting is respected too.

data.name: Help_Settings_Animations_When
data.value: Choose Reduced or Off if motion is distracting or on a slow or battery-saving system.

data.name: Help_Settings_Arguments_Risk
data.value: Some options are risky: skipping the compatibility check or allowing all power modes on battery can run features the laptop doesn't support; "allow all certificates" turns off HTTPS checks for update downloads. Changes apply on the next start.

data.name: Help_Settings_Arguments_What
data.value: Sets startup options normally passed on the command line, such as starting minimized, trace logging, a proxy, or skipping the compatibility check.

data.name: Help_Settings_Arguments_When
data.value: Mostly for troubleshooting or when support asks for a specific option.

data.name: Help_Settings_Autorun_What
data.value: Starts LLT minimized to the tray when you sign in to Windows, using a Windows scheduled task.

data.name: Help_Settings_Autorun_When
data.value: Keep it on if you rely on automations, hotkeys, the OSD or custom fan curves: they only work while LLT is running.

data.name: Help_Settings_Backdrop_Risk
data.value: Acrylic and Mica use slightly more GPU time and aren't available on every Windows version. Takes effect after LLT restarts.

data.name: Help_Settings_Backdrop_What
data.value: The Windows 11 effect behind the window: Mica, Acrylic, Tabbed or none.

data.name: Help_Settings_BackgroundImage_What
data.value: Shows a picture of your choice behind the app's content, with adjustable opacity and blur.

data.name: Help_Settings_Backup_Risk
data.value: A backup can contain automations that run programs. When restoring, LLT checks the file and lists such actions before applying it; only restore backups you made or trust.

data.name: Help_Settings_Backup_What
data.value: Saves all LLT settings, automations and presets to one file, or restores them from such a file.

data.name: Help_Settings_Backup_When
data.value: Before resetting Windows, moving to a new laptop, or trying risky changes.

data.name: Help_Settings_BootLogo_Risk
data.value: LLT writes the image to the EFI system partition and sets a firmware variable. A wrong size or format is refused; if a BIOS update or reset brings the default back, set it again.

data.name: Help_Settings_BootLogo_What
data.value: Replaces the Lenovo/Legion logo shown while the laptop starts with your own image, or puts the original back.

data.name: Help_Settings_CheckUpdates_What
data.value: Checks now whether a newer LLT version is available on the selected channel.

data.name: Help_Settings_CLI_Risk
data.value: Any program running as you can then change LLT settings through it. Leave it off if you don't use it.

data.name: Help_Settings_CLI_What
data.value: Lets the llt command-line tool control the running app (power mode, features, quick actions).

data.name: Help_Settings_CLI_When
data.value: For scripts, Stream Deck buttons or other tools that run commands.

data.name: Help_Settings_CLIPath_What
data.value: Adds LLT's folder to your user PATH so you can type llt in any terminal. New terminals pick it up.

data.name: Help_Settings_CompactMode_What
data.value: Uses tighter spacing so more cards fit on the screen at once.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableLegionSpace_Risk
data.value: Legion Space's own features stop working while disabled.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableLegionSpace_What
data.value: Stops Legion Space and its service without uninstalling it.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableLegionSpace_When
data.value: When Legion Space overrides LLT's settings.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableLegionZone_Risk
data.value: Legion Zone's own features stop working while disabled.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableLegionZone_What
data.value: Stops Legion Zone and its service without uninstalling it.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableLegionZone_When
data.value: When Legion Zone overrides LLT's power mode or lighting.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableLenovoHotkeys_Risk
data.value: Fn keys LLT doesn't know may stop doing anything until the service is enabled again.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableLenovoHotkeys_What
data.value: Stops the Lenovo Hotkeys service; LLT then handles the Fn shortcuts itself.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableVantage_Risk
data.value: Vantage features stop working while disabled, including Lenovo's driver and BIOS update checks. Get updates from Lenovo's support site instead.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableVantage_What
data.value: Stops Lenovo Vantage and its ImController service and their scheduled tasks, without uninstalling them. Turning it off starts them again.

data.name: Help_Settings_DisableVantage_When
data.value: When Vantage and LLT fight over the same settings (power mode, battery mode, keyboard light).

data.name: Help_Settings_ExcludeRefreshRates_What
data.value: Refresh rates ticked here are skipped when Fn+R cycles through them.

data.name: Help_Settings_FnQCustom_Risk
data.value: Custom mode applies your own limits, which may run hotter or louder than the built-in modes.

data.name: Help_Settings_FnQCustom_What
data.value: Adds Custom mode to the Fn+Q cycle, after the built-in modes.

data.name: Help_Settings_FnQCustom_When
data.value: When you use a Custom preset often and want to reach it from the keyboard.

data.name: Help_Settings_GameDetection_Risk
data.value: Detection only reads the list of running processes and GPU usage; it never opens or reads a game's memory.

data.name: Help_Settings_GameDetection_What
data.value: Chooses how LLT decides that a game is running: Automatic, a known-games list, Windows Game Mode, the discrete GPU being in use, or only processes you add. The result drives the "Games are running" and "Games stopped" automation triggers.

data.name: Help_Settings_GameDetection_When
data.value: Change it if those automations start for non-games (for example a video editor on the discrete GPU) or miss your games.

data.name: Help_Settings_HardwareAcceleration_Risk
data.value: On hybrid-graphics laptops it can cause flicker or black flashes and may keep the discrete GPU awake, using more battery. Restart LLT after changing it.

data.name: Help_Settings_HardwareAcceleration_What
data.value: Draws the LLT window with the GPU instead of the CPU.

data.name: Help_Settings_HardwareAcceleration_When
data.value: Leave it off unless the window feels slow to draw.

data.name: Help_Settings_HardwareSensors_Risk
data.value: Uses a kernel-mode driver and a little more CPU. Some anti-cheat software dislikes drivers like this; game-safe mode pauses these reads while a protected game runs, but the driver itself stays installed.

data.name: Help_Settings_HardwareSensors_What
data.value: Reads detailed sensors (CPU package power, per-core clocks and voltages, RAM and disk temperatures) through LibreHardwareMonitor and the PawnIO driver. Without it, LLT still shows the basic temperatures, usage and fan speeds Lenovo's firmware reports.

data.name: Help_Settings_HardwareSensors_When
data.value: When you want the full sensor dashboard or detailed OSD values.

data.name: Help_Settings_HWiNFO_Risk
data.value: Writes the values to your user registry while it runs. Restart HWiNFO64 after changing this.

data.name: Help_Settings_HWiNFO_What
data.value: Publishes values only LLT can read (fan speeds, battery temperature and more) as custom sensors in HWiNFO64, refreshed every second.

data.name: Help_Settings_HWiNFO_When
data.value: When you log or graph sensors in HWiNFO64.

data.name: Help_Settings_KeyDiscovery_What
data.value: Listens while you press keys and shows special keys LLT doesn't know yet, so you can give them an action.

data.name: Help_Settings_Language_What
data.value: The language of LLT's text. Text not yet translated appears in English. LLT reloads its window to apply it.

data.name: Help_Settings_LockWindowSize_What
data.value: Stops the main window from being resized by dragging its edges.

data.name: Help_Settings_Logging_Risk
data.value: Logs grow over time and may include your laptop model, settings and process names. Turn it off afterwards.

data.name: Help_Settings_Logging_What
data.value: Writes a detailed log of what LLT does to its log folder, for reporting problems.

data.name: Help_Settings_Logging_When
data.value: Turn it on, reproduce the problem, then attach the log to a bug report.

data.name: Help_Settings_MinimizeOnClose_What
data.value: The window's close button hides LLT to the tray instead of quitting it. Quit from the tray icon's menu.

data.name: Help_Settings_MinimizeOnClose_When
data.value: Useful when you close windows out of habit but want automations and hotkeys to keep working.

data.name: Help_Settings_MinimizeToTray_What
data.value: Minimizing the window hides it in the notification area (tray) instead of the taskbar. LLT keeps running.

data.name: Help_Settings_NeonGlow_Risk
data.value: Strong glow uses a little more GPU time to draw the window.

data.name: Help_Settings_NeonGlow_What
data.value: How strongly selected and active items glow in the Neon style.

data.name: Help_Settings_NewSensorDashboard_What
data.value: Switches the dashboard's sensor area between the newer, configurable layout and the original one. Both show the same readings.

data.name: Help_Settings_Notifications_What
data.value: Opens the list of on-screen notifications (Fn keys, power mode, updates, automations and more), where each can be turned on or off and positioned.

data.name: Help_Settings_OnBatterySinceReset_What
data.value: Starts the Battery page's "On battery since" counter over each time Windows starts, instead of only when the charger is connected.

data.name: Help_Settings_Osd_Risk
data.value: FPS uses Windows' own event tracing (ETW). While an anti-cheat game runs, game-safe mode limits the OSD to driver-free sources.

data.name: Help_Settings_Osd_What
data.value: A small always-on-top window showing live values such as FPS, temperatures and usage. It is a separate window drawn over the game; LLT never injects into or hooks the game.

data.name: Help_Settings_Osd_When
data.value: While gaming or benchmarking. Toggle it with your hotkey or an Fn quick action.

data.name: Help_Settings_PowerPlansControlPanel_What
data.value: Opens Windows' classic Power Options, where each power plan's sleep, screen-off and processor settings are edited.

data.name: Help_Settings_RememberWindowPosition_What
data.value: Opens the window where it was last time instead of centered on the screen.

data.name: Help_Settings_Reset_Risk
data.value: Cannot be undone. Make a backup first if you might want anything back.

data.name: Help_Settings_Reset_What
data.value: Deletes every LLT setting, automation and Custom mode preset and restarts the app with defaults.

data.name: Help_Settings_Reset_When
data.value: When settings are broken and you want a clean start.

data.name: Help_Settings_RetroEffects_What
data.value: Strength of the scanlines and the soft glow around text in the Retro style.

data.name: Help_Settings_RetroEffects_When
data.value: Lower them if text is hard to read.

data.name: Help_Settings_RetroPhosphor_What
data.value: The screen color of the Retro style, like the phosphor of an old CRT monitor (green, amber or white).

data.name: Help_Settings_Skin_What
data.value: The overall look of the app: Fluent (the standard Windows look), Neon or Retro. Only the appearance changes; every feature works the same.

data.name: Help_Settings_SmartFnLock_What
data.value: While Fn Lock is on, holding Alt, Ctrl or Shift temporarily turns it off, so shortcuts like Alt+F4 work without pressing Fn.

data.name: Help_Settings_SmartKeys_What
data.value: Lists the laptop's special keys and lets you choose what each one does: its default action, a quick action, or nothing.

data.name: Help_Settings_SyncBrightness_What
data.value: When you change brightness, LLT copies the level to every Windows power plan, so switching power mode (which can switch plans) doesn't change brightness.

data.name: Help_Settings_SyncBrightness_When
data.value: When brightness jumps after Fn+Q or plugging in the charger.

data.name: Help_Settings_Theme_What
data.value: Light, dark, or follow the Windows app theme.

data.name: Help_Settings_UpdateChannel_Risk
data.value: Beta and Dev builds are less tested and may have bugs.

data.name: Help_Settings_UpdateChannel_What
data.value: Stable gets tested releases; Beta and Dev get newer builds earlier.

data.name: Help_Settings_UpdateFrequency_What
data.value: How often LLT looks for a new version in the background.

data.name: Help_Settings_UpdateMethod_What
data.value: How a new version is downloaded and installed once one is found.

data.name: Help_SpecialKeys_HiddenKey_What
data.value: A key you hid from the list. It keeps its action. Right-click to show it again.

data.name: Help_SpecialKeys_Key_What
data.value: A special key on this laptop and what it currently does. Click to change its action; right-click to hide it from the list.

data.name: Help_SpecialKeys_Label_What
data.value: A name for this key, shown in the special keys list.

data.name: Help_SpecialKeys_Mode_What
data.value: What happens when this key is pressed: its normal action, a quick action you choose, or nothing.

data.name: Help_Battery_Current_What
data.value: Energy stored in the battery right now, in watt-hours.

data.name: Help_Battery_Cycles_What
data.value: Full charge-discharge cycles counted by the battery. Two half discharges count as one cycle.

data.name: Help_Battery_Design_What
data.value: Energy the battery held when new, in watt-hours.

data.name: Help_Battery_FirstUse_What
data.value: When the battery was first used, as reported by the battery.

data.name: Help_Battery_Full_What
data.value: Energy the battery holds when full today, in watt-hours. Drops slowly as the battery ages.

data.name: Help_Battery_Health_What
data.value: Full-charge capacity as a percentage of design capacity.

data.name: Help_Battery_Health_When
data.value: Some loss per year is normal. A sudden large drop may mean the battery needs calibrating or replacing.

data.name: Help_Battery_ManufactureDate_What
data.value: When the battery was made, as reported by the battery.

data.name: Help_Battery_MaxRate_What
data.value: The highest charge or drain rate seen since the battery last switched between charging and draining (or since LLT started).

data.name: Help_Battery_MinRate_What
data.value: The lowest charge or drain rate seen since the battery last switched between charging and draining (or since LLT started).

data.name: Help_Battery_OnBatterySince_Risk
data.value: Can be inaccurate if the laptop was charged while off.

data.name: Help_Battery_OnBatterySince_What
data.value: Time since the charger was last disconnected.

data.name: Help_Battery_Rate_What
data.value: How fast the battery is charging (+) or draining (−) right now, in watts.

data.name: Help_Battery_Rate_When
data.value: Watch it while closing apps to find what drains the battery.

data.name: Help_Battery_Temperature_What
data.value: Battery temperature reported by the firmware.

data.name: Help_Battery_Temperature_When
data.value: Batteries age faster when they're often above about 40 °C; Conservation mode and good airflow help.

data.name: Help_Dashboard_DiscreteGpu_Risk
data.value: Apps using the discrete GPU may crash or close and lose unsaved work. Only works in hybrid mode.

data.name: Help_Dashboard_DiscreteGpu_What
data.value: Shows whether the discrete GPU is active and which apps keep it awake. Deactivate briefly restarts the discrete GPU so it can go back to sleep; Kill apps closes the apps using it.

data.name: Help_Dashboard_DiscreteGpu_When
data.value: When battery drains fast because an app keeps the discrete GPU awake for no reason.

data.name: Help_Dashboard_OverclockDiscreteGpu_Risk
data.value: Too high an offset causes crashes, graphical artifacts or driver resets. Raise in small steps and test each step.

data.name: Help_Dashboard_OverclockDiscreteGpu_What
data.value: Applies the discrete GPU clock offsets set in its settings (gear button). The toggle turns the overclock on or off.

data.name: Help_Dashboard_TurnOffMonitors_What
data.value: Turns off all displays right away, without sleeping or locking. Moving the mouse or pressing a key wakes them.

data.name: Help_Dashboard_TurnOffMonitors_When
data.value: During long downloads or renders, or to save power when stepping away. Lock the PC separately if needed.

data.name: Help_DiscreteGpu_KeepAwake_Risk
data.value: Uses more power and reduces battery life noticeably.

data.name: Help_DiscreteGpu_KeepAwake_What
data.value: Keeps a small Direct3D connection open on the discrete GPU so it never powers down.

data.name: Help_DiscreteGpu_KeepAwake_When
data.value: If games or external displays stutter when the discrete GPU wakes up.

data.name: Help_DiscreteGpu_PState_Risk
data.value: A high P-state keeps clocks and power up even when idle, so more heat, fan noise and battery drain.

data.name: Help_DiscreteGpu_PState_What
data.value: Locks the discrete GPU to one performance state (P-state) through the NVIDIA driver, instead of letting it clock up and down. Auto returns control to the driver.

data.name: Help_DiscreteGpu_PState_When
data.value: To remove clock-change hiccups in latency-sensitive games or benchmarks.

data.name: Help_EditDashboard_Sensors_What
data.value: Shows or hides the sensor area on the dashboard.

data.name: Help_EditDashboard_StatusStrip_What
data.value: Shows or hides the live status strip and the large power-mode selector at the top of the dashboard.

data.name: Help_Feature_AlwaysOnUSBState_Risk
data.value: Drains the battery while the laptop is off if it isn't plugged in.

data.name: Help_Feature_AlwaysOnUSBState_What
data.value: Keeps power on a USB port while the laptop is off, sleeping or hibernated, so phones and other devices can charge.

data.name: Help_Feature_AutoColorManagementState_Risk
data.value: Some older apps and games can look slightly different with it on.

data.name: Help_Feature_AutoColorManagementState_What
data.value: Windows' Auto Color Management: Windows manages colors system-wide using the display's color profile, for more accurate colors.

data.name: Help_Feature_BatteryNightChargeState_What
data.value: When plugged in overnight, the battery charges to 80% and finishes to 100% around the time you usually start using the laptop. Windows and the firmware decide the timing.

data.name: Help_Feature_BatteryNightChargeState_When
data.value: If the laptop charges overnight every night.

data.name: Help_Feature_BatteryState_Risk
data.value: Rapid Charge warms the battery and wears it slightly faster when used all the time. Conservation means less runtime when you unplug.

data.name: Help_Feature_BatteryState_What
data.value: How the battery charges. Conservation stops charging well below full (the exact level depends on the model) to slow battery wear. Normal charges to 100%. Rapid Charge charges faster on the charger.

data.name: Help_Feature_BatteryState_When
data.value: Conservation if the laptop stays plugged in most of the time; Normal before travelling; Rapid Charge when you need charge quickly.

data.name: Help_Feature_DpiScale_Risk
data.value: Some apps look blurry until they're restarted after a scale change.

data.name: Help_Feature_DpiScale_What
data.value: Windows' display scaling (text and icon size) for the built-in display.

data.name: Help_Feature_FlipToStartState_What
data.value: Turns the laptop on when you open the lid.

data.name: Help_Feature_FnLockState_What
data.value: When on, F1–F12 do their special functions (volume, brightness…) without holding Fn; hold Fn for the plain F keys.

data.name: Help_Feature_HDRState_What
data.value: Turns Windows HDR on or off for the built-in display, where supported.

data.name: Help_Feature_HDRState_When
data.value: On for HDR games and videos; off for accurate colors in normal apps and slightly better battery life.

data.name: Help_Feature_HybridModeState_Risk
data.value: Switching needs a restart, and LLT asks first. Discrete-only uses much more battery. Integrated-only turns the discrete GPU off, so games run slowly and ports wired to it may not work.

data.name: Help_Feature_HybridModeState_What
data.value: How the integrated and discrete GPUs work together. Hybrid lets Windows use the efficient integrated GPU and wake the discrete one when needed; discrete-only routes everything through the discrete GPU; some models add an automatic mode or integrated-only.

data.name: Help_Feature_HybridModeState_When
data.value: Hybrid for battery life; discrete-only for the lowest latency and highest frame rate on the laptop screen.

data.name: Help_Feature_InstantBootState_What
data.value: Turns the laptop on automatically when the charger is connected.

data.name: Help_Feature_ITSMode_Risk
data.value: Performance modes run hotter and louder.

data.name: Help_Feature_ITSMode_What
data.value: Lenovo's Intelligent Thermal Solution mode, used instead of power modes on some models: it sets fan behavior and power limits for quiet, balanced or performance use.

data.name: Help_Feature_ITSMode_When
data.value: Quieter modes for office work and battery; performance modes for games and heavy work.

data.name: Help_Feature_MicrophoneState_What
data.value: Mutes or unmutes every microphone through Windows. Apps see the microphone as muted.

data.name: Help_Feature_OneLevelWhiteKeyboardBacklightState_What
data.value: Turns the white keyboard backlight on or off (this keyboard has a single brightness level).

data.name: Help_Feature_OverDriveState_Risk
data.value: On some panels it causes faint bright or dark trails (overshoot). Turn it off if you see them.

data.name: Help_Feature_OverDriveState_What
data.value: Panel overdrive drives the display's pixels harder so they change faster, reducing blur and ghosting in motion.

data.name: Help_Feature_PanelLogoBacklightState_What
data.value: Turns the light of the logo on the lid on or off.

data.name: Help_Feature_PortsBacklightState_What
data.value: Turns the lights of the rear ports on or off.

data.name: Help_Feature_RefreshRate_What
data.value: How many times per second the built-in display refreshes. Fn+R also cycles it.

data.name: Help_Feature_RefreshRate_When
data.value: Highest for games and smooth scrolling; 60 Hz to save battery.

data.name: Help_Feature_Resolution_What
data.value: The built-in display's resolution, same as Windows display settings.

data.name: Help_Feature_Resolution_When
data.value: Lower it for more frame rate in demanding games.

data.name: Help_Feature_TouchpadLockState_What
data.value: Turns the touchpad off so it can't be touched by accident, for example while gaming with a mouse.

data.name: Help_Feature_WhiteKeyboardBacklightState_What
data.value: Brightness of the white keyboard backlight (off, low or high).

data.name: Help_Feature_WinKeyState_What
data.value: Disables the Windows key on the built-in keyboard so it can't open Start mid-game. External keyboards are not affected.

data.name: Help_GodMode_ApuSppt_Risk
data.value: Higher values mean more heat and fan noise.

data.name: Help_GodMode_ApuSppt_What
data.value: AMD's slow package power tracking limit: the sustained power the AMD processor may use, similar to Intel's PL1.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CoreCurve_Risk
data.value: An undervolt that is too strong causes random crashes, often only at idle or light load.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CoreCurve_What
data.value: Turns the All Core Curve Optimizer value on or off for this preset.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuCrossLoading_What
data.value: The sustained CPU power limit used when the GPU is also under heavy load, as in most games.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuCrossLoading_When
data.value: Lower it to leave more of the shared cooling and power budget to the GPU in games.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuPeak_Risk
data.value: Setting it beyond what the laptop's power delivery handles can cause sudden shutdowns under heavy load.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuPeak_What
data.value: The absolute cap for instant power spikes, protecting the CPU's power delivery.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuPL1_Risk
data.value: Higher values mean more heat and fan noise; the CPU still throttles at its temperature limit.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuPL1_What
data.value: PL1: the CPU power the laptop can sustain indefinitely, in watts. Sets most of the performance and heat in long loads.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuPL1_When
data.value: Raise it for long renders or compiles if temperatures allow; lower it for a quieter, cooler laptop.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuPL2_Risk
data.value: Higher bursts heat up the CPU quickly and spin the fans up.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuPL2_What
data.value: PL2: the higher power the CPU may use for short bursts (see the duration setting), in watts. Makes apps feel snappy.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuTau_Risk
data.value: Long durations with a high short-term limit heat the laptop up faster.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuTau_What
data.value: How long, in seconds, the CPU may stay at the short-term limit before falling back to the long-term limit.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuTemp_Risk
data.value: Higher limits let the CPU run hotter for longer; they never go past the CPU's own safety limit.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuTemp_What
data.value: The CPU temperature at which the firmware starts lowering CPU power to stay at or below it.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CpuTemp_When
data.value: Lower it for a cooler, quieter laptop (with less performance).

data.name: Help_GodMode_CurveOptimizer_Risk
data.value: Too negative causes random crashes or freezes, sometimes only at idle. Change in small steps and test for hours.

data.name: Help_GodMode_CurveOptimizer_What
data.value: AMD Curve Optimizer for all cores: a negative value lowers voltage at every clock (undervolting), reducing heat and often raising sustained clocks.

data.name: Help_GodMode_FanCurve_Risk
data.value: A flatter curve runs hotter. LLT won't accept points below the laptop's minimum, and the firmware still throttles at its temperature limits.

data.name: Help_GodMode_FanCurve_What
data.value: Fan level at each of the firmware's ten temperature steps, used while this Custom preset is active. The firmware picks the step from the hottest of the CPU, GPU and heatsink sensors.

data.name: Help_GodMode_FanMax_Risk
data.value: Loud, and more fan wear over long periods.

data.name: Help_GodMode_FanMax_What
data.value: Runs both fans at full speed all the time while this preset is active, ignoring the curve.

data.name: Help_GodMode_FanMax_When
data.value: Short heavy loads like benchmarks, or cooling down quickly.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuCtgp_Risk
data.value: Higher values mean more heat and fan noise and need the full-power charger.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuCtgp_What
data.value: Configurable TGP: the GPU's main sustained power limit, in watts. The biggest single factor for gaming performance.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuCtgp_When
data.value: Lower it for quieter gaming or on a weaker charger.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuDynamicBoost_Risk
data.value: More GPU power means more heat in the shared cooling system.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuDynamicBoost_What
data.value: NVIDIA Dynamic Boost: extra watts the GPU may take from the CPU's budget when the CPU isn't busy.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuTemp_Risk
data.value: Higher limits let the GPU run hotter; they never go past the GPU's own safety limit.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuTemp_What
data.value: The GPU temperature at which it starts lowering clocks to stay at or below it.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuToCpuBoost_What
data.value: The extra power the CPU may borrow from the GPU's budget when the GPU isn't busy.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuToCpuBoost_When
data.value: Set to 0 W to stop the CPU drawing extra power during GPU-heavy games, for less heat and noise.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuTpp_What
data.value: NVIDIA's Total Processing Power target on AC: the combined CPU power level above which the GPU driver starts shifting power between CPU and GPU. The value is an offset from the firmware's baseline, set through Lenovo's firmware.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuTpp_When
data.value: Lower it to keep the CPU from taking power the GPU could use in games.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuTppPcf_What
data.value: NVIDIA's Total Processing Power target on AC: the combined CPU power level above which the GPU driver starts shifting power between CPU and GPU. The value is an offset from the firmware's baseline, set through Lenovo's firmware. This variant is set through the NVIDIA driver (NVAPI) instead of Lenovo's firmware.

data.name: Help_GodMode_GpuTppPcf_When
data.value: Lower it to keep the CPU from taking power the GPU could use in games.

data.name: Help_GodMode_MaxOffset_Risk
data.value: None to the hardware: this can only lower the ceiling. A low ceiling limits performance.

data.name: Help_GodMode_MaxOffset_What
data.value: Lowers the upper end of the power and temperature sliders in this preset. It can't raise it: nothing above the maximum the firmware reports is ever sent to the laptop.

data.name: Help_GodMode_MinOffset_Risk
data.value: None to the hardware: this can only raise the floor. A high floor leaves less room to limit power or temperature.

data.name: Help_GodMode_MinOffset_What
data.value: Raises the lower end of the power and temperature sliders in this preset. It can't lower it: nothing below the minimum the firmware reports is ever sent to the laptop.

data.name: Help_GodMode_Overclocking_Risk
data.value: Wrong values can cause crashes, data loss from crashes, or a failed boot. Change one thing at a time and stress-test.

data.name: Help_GodMode_Overclocking_What
data.value: Turns on AMD Precision Boost Overdrive and Curve Optimizer settings for this preset (AMD CPUs that support it).

data.name: Help_GodMode_PboFrequency_Risk
data.value: Higher clocks can be unstable without enough voltage headroom; test for crashes.

data.name: Help_GodMode_PboFrequency_What
data.value: AMD PBO boost override: MHz allowed above the factory maximum boost clock.

data.name: Help_GodMode_PboScaler_Risk
data.value: Higher values may shorten the processor's life and increase heat. Stress-test after changes.

data.name: Help_GodMode_PboScaler_What
data.value: AMD PBO scaler: how far boost may push beyond the processor's factory reliability margins (1x = stock).

data.name: Help_GpuOc_Core_Risk
data.value: Too high causes crashes, artifacts or driver resets. Raise in small steps (for example +25 MHz) and test.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_Core_What
data.value: Adds (or removes) MHz to the GPU core clock at every point of NVIDIA's boost curve.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_Core_When
data.value: For a few percent more performance, or a negative offset for less heat.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_Memory_Risk
data.value: Unstable memory clocks show as flickering textures, crashes or lower performance from error correction. Test after every change.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_Memory_What
data.value: Raises or lowers the video memory clock, which changes memory bandwidth.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_VoltageCap_Risk
data.value: Too low a cap with a high core offset can crash games.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_VoltageCap_What
data.value: Caps the highest voltage (and so the clock) the GPU uses under load, while still letting it clock down at idle. A simple form of undervolting.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_VoltageCap_When
data.value: To lower temperature and fan noise for a small loss of peak performance.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_VoltageLock_Risk
data.value: The GPU no longer clocks down when idle: more power, heat and fan noise.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_VoltageLock_What
data.value: Locks the GPU to one voltage and its matching clock all the time.

data.name: Help_GpuOc_VoltageLock_When
data.value: For benchmarks or troubleshooting clock swings.

data.name: Help_Automation_Enable_What
data.value: Turns all automatic actions on or off. Quick actions you start yourself still work.

data.name: Help_Automation_Enable_When
data.value: Turn it off temporarily if something keeps changing your settings and you want to find out why.

data.name: Help_LampArray_Effect_Risk
data.value: If another app also controls the keyboard through Dynamic Lighting, they can override each other. Windows Settings > Personalization > Dynamic Lighting decides which app is in control.

data.name: Help_LampArray_Effect_What
data.value: The lighting effect LLT draws on the keyboard through Windows Dynamic Lighting.

data.name: Help_LampArray_Settings_What
data.value: General options for keyboards controlled through Windows Dynamic Lighting (LampArray), such as brightness.

data.name: Help_Macro_Enable_Risk
data.value: Macros watch the keyboard with a low-level hook and send simulated key presses. Some anti-cheat software and game rules don't allow that.

data.name: Help_Macro_Enable_What
data.value: Turns macros on or off. LLT must be running for macros to work; game-safe mode suspends them while a protected game runs.

data.name: Help_Macro_Event_What
data.value: One recorded input: a key or mouse button going down or up, or a mouse movement, followed by the pause recorded before the next one.

data.name: Help_Macro_IgnoreDelays_Risk
data.value: Some apps and games miss keys sent too quickly.

data.name: Help_Macro_IgnoreDelays_What
data.value: Plays the keys as fast as possible instead of with the pauses you recorded.

data.name: Help_Macro_Interrupt_What
data.value: Stops playback as soon as you press any other key.

data.name: Help_Macro_RecordingOptions_What
data.value: What is recorded: keyboard only, keyboard and mouse buttons, or all input including mouse movement.

data.name: Help_Macro_Repeat_What
data.value: How many times the recorded sequence plays each time its key is pressed.

data.name: Help_RgbKeyboard_Zone_What
data.value: The color of this part of the keyboard. The 4-zone keyboard is split into four areas from left to right.

data.name: Help_Spectrum_Brightness_What
data.value: Brightness of the per-key RGB keyboard, for all effects.

data.name: Help_Spectrum_Clockwise_What
data.value: Whether a rotating effect turns clockwise or counter-clockwise.

data.name: Help_Spectrum_ColorBoost_What
data.value: Brightens dim colors the way Lenovo Vantage does, so colors look the same as in Vantage.

data.name: Help_Spectrum_ColorBoostSettings_What
data.value: Fine-tunes the color boost: how much colors are brightened, the lowest level that is boosted, and when a color counts as white.

data.name: Help_Spectrum_Colors_What
data.value: The list of colors the effect cycles through.

data.name: Help_Spectrum_Direction_What
data.value: Which way the effect moves across the keyboard.

data.name: Help_Spectrum_Effect_What
data.value: The lighting animation, such as a static color, breathing, wave or rainbow; the list shows what this keyboard supports.

data.name: Help_Spectrum_EffectItem_What
data.value: One lighting effect in this profile and the keys it covers. Effects lower in the list are drawn over the ones above. Click to edit it.

data.name: Help_Step_AIEngineAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns Lenovo's AI Engine on or off; it shifts power between CPU and GPU automatically in supported games.

data.name: Help_Step_AirplaneModeAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns Windows airplane mode on or off (all wireless radios).

data.name: Help_Step_AlwaysOnUsbAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: Drains the battery while off if the laptop isn't plugged in.

data.name: Help_Step_AlwaysOnUsbAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets whether a USB port keeps powering devices while the laptop is off or asleep.

data.name: Help_Step_AutoColorManagementAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns Windows Auto Color Management on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_BatteryAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets the battery charging mode: Conservation, Normal or Rapid Charge.

data.name: Help_Step_BatteryAutomationStep_When
data.value: For example Conservation when the charger connects at your desk.

data.name: Help_Step_BatteryNightChargeAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns overnight battery charging (80% first, 100% by morning) on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_CloseAppAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: Everything that needs LLT running stops: other automations, hotkeys, the OSD, custom fan curves and game-safe mode.

data.name: Help_Step_CycleGodModePresetAutomationStep_What
data.value: Switches to the next Custom mode preset, and applies it right away if Custom mode is active.

data.name: Help_Step_DeactivateGPUAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: Apps using the discrete GPU may crash or close and lose unsaved work.

data.name: Help_Step_DeactivateGPUAutomationStep_What
data.value: Restarts the discrete GPU or closes the apps using it, so it can power down (same as the dashboard's Discrete GPU card).

data.name: Help_Step_DeactivateGPUAutomationStep_When
data.value: For example when unplugging the charger.

data.name: Help_Step_DelayAutomationStep_What
data.value: Waits the given number of seconds before the next action.

data.name: Help_Step_DelayAutomationStep_When
data.value: When a device or setting needs a moment to settle, for example after a display connects.

data.name: Help_Step_DpiScaleAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: Some apps look blurry until restarted after a scale change.

data.name: Help_Step_DpiScaleAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets Windows' display scaling for the built-in display.

data.name: Help_Step_FanMaxSpeedAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: Loud; long use increases fan wear.

data.name: Help_Step_FanMaxSpeedAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns full fan speed on, off, or toggles it.

data.name: Help_Step_FanMaxSpeedAutomationStep_When
data.value: For example on when a benchmark starts and off when it ends.

data.name: Help_Step_FlipToStartAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets whether opening the lid turns the laptop on.

data.name: Help_Step_FnLockAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns Fn Lock on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_GodModePresetAutomationStep_What
data.value: Selects a specific Custom mode preset (and applies it if Custom mode is active).

data.name: Help_Step_GodModePresetAutomationStep_When
data.value: For example a quiet preset when a video app starts.

data.name: Help_Step_HardwareSensorsAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns detailed hardware sensors (PawnIO driver) on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_HardwareSensorsAutomationStep_When
data.value: Off when unplugging to save a little power, on when gaming.

data.name: Help_Step_HDRAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns Windows HDR on or off for the built-in display.

data.name: Help_Step_HybridModeAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: Most changes need a restart; LLT asks before restarting.

data.name: Help_Step_HybridModeAutomationStep_What
data.value: Changes the GPU working mode (hybrid, discrete-only…).

data.name: Help_Step_InstantBootAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets whether connecting the charger turns the laptop on.

data.name: Help_Step_ITSModeAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets the ITS mode (on laptops that use ITS instead of power modes).

data.name: Help_Step_MacroAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: Macros send simulated key presses, which some anti-cheats and game rules don't allow.

data.name: Help_Step_MacroAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns macros on, off, or toggles them.

data.name: Help_Step_MacroAutomationStep_When
data.value: For example off when a protected game starts.

data.name: Help_Step_NotificationAutomationStep_What
data.value: Shows an on-screen notification with your text.

data.name: Help_Step_NotificationAutomationStep_When
data.value: To confirm that an automation ran.

data.name: Help_Step_OneLevelWhiteKeyboardBacklightAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns the single-level white keyboard backlight on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_OsdAutomationStep_What
data.value: Shows, hides or toggles the on-screen display. This is what the "Toggle OSD" quick action uses.

data.name: Help_Step_OsdLockPositionAutomationStep_What
data.value: Locks the OSD in place (clicks pass through it) or unlocks it so it can be dragged.

data.name: Help_Step_OverclockDiscreteGPUAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: An unstable overclock can crash games or reset the driver.

data.name: Help_Step_OverclockDiscreteGPUAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns the discrete GPU overclock on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_OverclockDiscreteGPUAutomationStep_When
data.value: For example on when games run and off otherwise.

data.name: Help_Step_OverDriveAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns panel overdrive on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_PanelLogoBacklightAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns the lid logo light on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_PlaySoundAutomationStep_When
data.value: As an audible confirmation that an automation ran.

data.name: Help_Step_PortsBacklightAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns the rear ports light on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_PowerModeAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets the power mode (Quiet, Balance, Performance, Custom…).

data.name: Help_Step_PowerModeAutomationStep_When
data.value: For example Performance when games start and Balance when they stop.

data.name: Help_Step_QuickActionAutomationStep_What
data.value: Runs the actions of another quick action, so shared actions are kept in one place.

data.name: Help_Step_RefreshRateAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets the built-in display's refresh rate.

data.name: Help_Step_RefreshRateAutomationStep_When
data.value: For example 60 Hz on battery and the highest rate on the charger.

data.name: Help_Step_RGBKeyboardBacklightAutomationStep_What
data.value: Selects a 4-zone RGB keyboard preset (or turns the backlight off).

data.name: Help_Step_RunAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: The program runs with LLT's permissions, which are administrator rights. Only run programs you trust, and keep their files where other users can't replace them.

data.name: Help_Step_RunAutomationStep_What
data.value: Starts a program or script with optional arguments; it can run hidden, wait until it finishes, or skip starting it if it's already running.

data.name: Help_Step_RunAutomationStep_When
data.value: To start or stop your own tools along with other changes.

data.name: Help_Step_SpectrumKeyboardBacklightBrightnessAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets the per-key RGB keyboard brightness.

data.name: Help_Step_SpectrumKeyboardBacklightImportProfileAutomationStep_Risk
data.value: Replaces the effects saved in the current slot.

data.name: Help_Step_SpectrumKeyboardBacklightImportProfileAutomationStep_What
data.value: Loads a per-key RGB lighting profile from a file into the current profile slot.

data.name: Help_Step_SpectrumKeyboardBacklightProfileAutomationStep_What
data.value: Switches the per-key RGB keyboard to one of its profile slots.

data.name: Help_Step_TouchpadLockAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns the touchpad on or off.

data.name: Help_Step_TouchpadLockAutomationStep_When
data.value: For example off when a mouse is connected.

data.name: Help_Step_TurnOffMonitorsAutomationStep_What
data.value: Turns off all displays (they wake on mouse or keyboard input).

data.name: Help_Step_WhiteKeyboardBacklightAutomationStep_What
data.value: Sets the white keyboard backlight level.

data.name: Help_Step_WinKeyAutomationStep_What
data.value: Enables or disables the Windows key on the built-in keyboard.

data.name: Help_Trigger_ACAdapterConnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the charger is connected.

data.name: Help_Trigger_ACAdapterDisconnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the charger is disconnected.

data.name: Help_Trigger_ACAdapterDisconnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_When
data.value: For example to switch to Quiet and 60 Hz on battery.

data.name: Help_Trigger_AndAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when all of the combined triggers are true at the same time.

data.name: Help_Trigger_BatteryPercentageAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the battery charge crosses the percentage you set.

data.name: Help_Trigger_BatteryPercentageAutomationPipelineTrigger_When
data.value: For example to turn on battery saving below 20%.

data.name: Help_Trigger_DeviceConnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when a chosen device (for example a mouse, controller or dock) is connected.

data.name: Help_Trigger_DeviceDisconnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when a chosen device is disconnected.

data.name: Help_Trigger_DisplayOffAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when Windows turns the displays off.

data.name: Help_Trigger_DisplayOnAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when Windows turns the displays on.

data.name: Help_Trigger_ExternalDisplayConnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when an external display is connected.

data.name: Help_Trigger_ExternalDisplayDisconnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when an external display is disconnected.

data.name: Help_Trigger_GamesAreRunningAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when a game starts, as decided by the game detection setting.

data.name: Help_Trigger_GamesAreRunningAutomationPipelineTrigger_When
data.value: To switch to Performance, disable the Windows key and similar.

data.name: Help_Trigger_GamesStopAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the last detected game closes.

data.name: Help_Trigger_GodModePresetChangedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when a specific Custom mode preset becomes active.

data.name: Help_Trigger_HDROffAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when HDR is turned off.

data.name: Help_Trigger_HDROnAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when HDR is turned on.

data.name: Help_Trigger_HybridModeAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the GPU working mode becomes the one you choose, and at LLT startup if it already is.

data.name: Help_Trigger_LidClosedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the lid is closed (while the laptop stays awake, for example with an external display).

data.name: Help_Trigger_LidOpenedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the lid is opened.

data.name: Help_Trigger_LowWattageACAdapterConnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when a charger too weak to power the laptop at full load is connected (for example a USB-C charger).

data.name: Help_Trigger_LowWattageACAdapterConnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_When
data.value: To lower power limits so the battery doesn't drain while plugged in.

data.name: Help_Trigger_OnResumeAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the laptop wakes from sleep or hibernation.

data.name: Help_Trigger_OnResumeAutomationPipelineTrigger_When
data.value: To re-apply settings the firmware resets on wake.

data.name: Help_Trigger_OnStartupAutomationPipelineTrigger_Risk
data.value: Actions marked unsafe at startup (such as quitting LLT) are skipped here so LLT can't lock itself out.

data.name: Help_Trigger_OrAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when any one of the combined triggers happens.

data.name: Help_Trigger_PeriodicAutomationPipelineTrigger_Risk
data.value: Short intervals with heavy actions use CPU and battery.

data.name: Help_Trigger_PeriodicAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs repeatedly at the interval you set.

data.name: Help_Trigger_PowerModeAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the laptop switches to the power mode you choose, from Fn+Q, the dashboard or another automation.

data.name: Help_Trigger_PowerModeAutomationPipelineTrigger_When
data.value: To change the refresh rate or keyboard light with the mode.

data.name: Help_Trigger_ProcessesAreRunningAutomationPipelineTrigger_Risk
data.value: LLT only watches the list of running processes; it doesn't open or read them.

data.name: Help_Trigger_ProcessesAreRunningAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when one of the programs you list starts.

data.name: Help_Trigger_ProcessesStopRunningAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when all of the programs you list have closed.

data.name: Help_Trigger_TimeAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs at a set time of day, or at sunrise or sunset, optionally only on the days you choose.

data.name: Help_Trigger_TimeRangeAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Is true between two times of day; useful combined with other triggers.

data.name: Help_Trigger_TimeRangeAutomationPipelineTrigger_When
data.value: For example quiet fans only during the night.

data.name: Help_Trigger_UserInactivityAutomationPipelineTrigger_Risk
data.value: None to games: LLT checks Windows' own last-input time once a second and doesn't hook the keyboard or mouse.

data.name: Help_Trigger_UserInactivityAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs after you haven't used the mouse or keyboard for the time you set.

data.name: Help_Trigger_WiFiConnectedAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when Wi-Fi connects (optionally only to the networks you list).

data.name: Help_Osd_BackgroundColor_What
data.value: The color behind the OSD's values.

data.name: Help_Osd_CategoryColor_What
data.value: The color of group names such as CPU, GPU and FPS.

data.name: Help_Osd_CornerRadius_What
data.value: How rounded the OSD's top and bottom corners are.

data.name: Help_Osd_CriticalColor_What
data.value: The color of values that passed their critical threshold (Thresholds tab).

data.name: Help_Osd_FontSize_What
data.value: The size of the OSD's text.

data.name: Help_Osd_FpsRedline_What
data.value: The lowest frame rate you find acceptable. Below it, the FPS value turns the critical color.

data.name: Help_Osd_LabelColor_What
data.value: The color of value names such as "Temp" or "Usage".

data.name: Help_Osd_LockPosition_What
data.value: Locks the OSD where it is: clicks pass through it to the game or app below. Unlock it to drag it somewhere else.

data.name: Help_Osd_LowFpsDelta_What
data.value: The largest gap you accept between average FPS and the 1% low. A bigger gap means stutter; the value then turns the critical color.

data.name: Help_Osd_Opacity_What
data.value: How see-through the OSD's background is.

data.name: Help_Osd_OverlayStyle_What
data.value: The layout of the on-screen display: Panel (a block of rows) or Bar (one horizontal line, good along a screen edge).

data.name: Help_Osd_RefreshInterval_Risk
data.value: Very short intervals use a little more CPU, which can cost a few FPS on weak CPUs.

data.name: Help_Osd_RefreshInterval_What
data.value: How often the OSD's values update.

data.name: Help_Osd_SnapThreshold_What
data.value: How close (in pixels) the OSD must be dragged to a screen edge or corner before it snaps to it (both edges at once snaps it into the corner). 0 turns snapping off.

data.name: Help_Osd_TempCritical_What
data.value: Temperature (°C) at which CPU and GPU temperatures turn the critical color.

data.name: Help_Osd_TempWarning_What
data.value: Temperature (°C) at which CPU and GPU temperatures turn the warning color.

data.name: Help_Osd_UsageCritical_What
data.value: Usage (%) at which CPU, GPU and memory usage turn the critical color.

data.name: Help_Osd_UsageWarning_What
data.value: Usage (%) at which CPU, GPU and memory usage turn the warning color.

data.name: Help_Osd_WarningColor_What
data.value: The color of values that passed their warning threshold (Thresholds tab).

data.name: Help_Automation_Pipeline_What
data.value: One automation or quick action: what starts it (for automations) and the actions it runs, top to bottom. Expand it to edit, reorder or delete actions.

data.name: Help_Automation_Pipeline_When
data.value: Automations run on their own when their trigger happens; quick actions run when you start them from the tray, a special key or another action.

data.name: Help_EditDashboard_Group_What
data.value: A group of cards on the dashboard. Rename it, move it up or down, and add, remove or reorder its cards.

data.name: Help_RgbKeyboard_RGBKeyboardBacklightBrightness_What
data.value: Brightness of the 4-zone RGB keyboard for this preset.

data.name: Help_RgbKeyboard_RGBKeyboardBacklightEffect_What
data.value: The lighting effect of this preset: static zone colors, breathing, a smooth color cycle, or a wave moving left or right.

data.name: Help_RgbKeyboard_RGBKeyboardBacklightSpeed_What
data.value: How fast the effect animates. Static colors ignore it.

data.name: Help_Trigger_ITSModeAutomationPipelineTrigger_What
data.value: Runs when the laptop switches to the ITS mode you choose (on laptops that use ITS instead of power modes).

data.name: Osd_GameSafeBadge_Tooltip
data.value: An anti-cheat service is running, so the OSD shows only readings that need no driver. Values that need the hardware-sensor driver show a dash until the game closes.
